subject: Demote
claim: A Demote on the last placements can swap the Ghost into the leader's cult, costing a member, 5 followers and contest leads with no reply possible.
evidence: Cal's Demote at [213] swapped Dee's Regulars for Ghost and cost Dee about 18 followers (Ghost -5, Regulars 1 printed and 2 round-end, two contests from outright to tied), more than Ben's 8-point winning margin.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: Late in the game several rival cards aim at whoever leads on members, and the leader can answer almost none of them.
evidence: Mutineers, Repossessors, Demote with Ghost, Con Men and Protesters took about 30 followers off Dee in rounds II and III; she led by 18 after round II and lost by 8, answering only one (buying Copyist back).

subject: Last Call
claim: Taking Last Call first in a round skips your middle turns, so you end up placing the round's last minions in a row whatever happens to the token.
evidence: Ben took Last Call first in rounds II and III and placed the last three minions both times; Ava and Cal took the token from him and it changed nothing, and round II took him from 4 to 37.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: Spoilsport cancels a contest after all placements, and at game end its holder, if out of the race, picks who loses 10.
evidence: Cal, on 53 and out of the race, cancelled Went last and took 10 from Ben; Ben still won 82 to 74, and the card was public from Cal's second placement of round III.

subject: Test Drive
claim: Test Drive can fire a shop member's effect, such as Purifiers, against every rival after they have placed, from a round I outer-ring space.
evidence: Ava's last placement of round I took a member each from Ben and Dee (Cal's was a borrowed one, so free) and paid her 4 resources, but no round I prize moved and Purifiers had been face up since her first placement.

subject: Most members of one color
claim: Red's one-color contest and Blue's Most members reward the same pile of bodies, so one swap moves both and the same player tends to win both.
evidence: Dee won both in rounds I and II, and Cal and Dee tied both in round III.

subject: Dabblers
claim: Dabblers, a 5-cost member counting as 2, decides the members contests and gets passed around by every swap.
evidence: It gave Dee round I's Red and Blue leads 3 to 2 and changed hands three times in round II (Dee, Cal, Ava, Cal).

subject: Most minions on green
claim: The Green contest went uncontested in rounds I and II, but a player who placed for it took it.
evidence: Rivals put 1 minion on Green in each of rounds I and II and Dee won +4 and +6; in round III Ava used Protesters and two placements and won it 3 to 2 for +10.

subject: Buying followers
claim: Turns that leave 1 to 4 resources push you to spend a recruit on 1 follower.
evidence: Cal made 9 of the game's 11 one-follower buys because his free-recruit spaces gave members, not resources; Ava and Ben made 1 each and Dee none.

subject: Buying followers
claim: Buying followers every turn beat building a cult.
evidence: Ben and Ava bought 46 each, but second place Dee bought 0 off 40 contest followers, and Ben's 4 members paid him 11 followers and 13 resources; the 10-pack gives the same 1 follower per resource as the 5-pack.

subject: Picket Line
claim: A cheap round I purple member looks like a 1-follower trap but pays all game.
evidence: Picket Line paid 7 purple from rival Purple placements and counted for Night Managers twice and Timekeeper once; Ben called it close to worthless.

subject: Night Managers
claim: Night Managers pays well for a player who places the round's last minion.
evidence: Bought from the discard pile for 4, it paid 3 and 4 followers plus 1 printed, and still paid in round III when Spoilsport cancelled Went last.

subject: Last-Minute Shopper
claim: Last-Minute Shopper's round-end blue and extra recruit is a steady engine.
evidence: For 5 resources it paid 9 blue and three extra recruits, each a 5-follower buy, over the game.

subject: Blue Cloak
claim: The Blue Cloak turns every shop-clearing space into income and paid far more than the other cloaks.
evidence: It paid 20 resources, against the Green Cloak 14, Purple Cloak 10 and Red Cloak 9.

subject: Blue Cloak
claim: The Blue Cloak's text does not say whether discarding shop members counts.
evidence: Ben passed on it at the cloak pick because of this and only understood it when Ava's discards paid her 7 resources in round I.

subject: Green Cloak
claim: "+2 of its color" on the Green Cloak reads as green to a new player, though it pays the copied action's color.
evidence: At [78] Dee expected green from copying Recruit Twice, got blue, and could not afford the Copyist she had planned that turn.

subject: Agents
claim: Agents stops its owner's own copies, as printed, and a new player bought it without seeing that.
evidence: Dee's Reprise at [162] got nothing because her own Agents protected her Cover, costing a placement that could have copied Initiation for a free member up to 10.

subject: Echo
claim: Echo can copy a rival's big swap back one turn later.
evidence: Ava's Demote of Dabblers at [87] was Echoed by Cal at [90] with Echo open and Cal next to act; Cal called it the best interaction of the game.

subject: Echo
claim: Green's copy spaces let copy chains build a whole round, and they were the most enjoyed turns of the game.
evidence: Dee's round II copies of Recruit Twice, Crowd and Late Shift brought her six members and 18 contest followers.

subject: Con Men
claim: Con Men looks dead late when everyone spends to zero, but it punishes anyone who saves.
evidence: Ben called it dead at [182]; seven placements later Ava's Test Drive used it to take the 5 blue Dee had saved by passing.

subject: Protesters
claim: Protesters blocking one space can decide a contest.
evidence: Ava blocked Greatest Hits and took the last Green space herself: +10 instead of a +5 tie, and 5 fewer for Dee.

subject: Promote
claim: Promote can swap a rival's member out for a shop card and break their contest lead and their member conditions.
evidence: Ben's Promote of Cal's Loyalists for Closer turned Cal's sole Red lead into a three-way tie (+5 to Ben) and switched off Cal's Purists (-3).

subject: Late Shift
claim: Late Shift gives a free member and still leaves your normal recruit, and its cap grows with placements.
evidence: Late Shift and its copies brought in 4 free members, including an 8-cost Thrift Hunters for Dee through Fan Club.

subject: Crunch Time
claim: Crunch Time's three placements in a row let a trailing player chain free recruits before anyone answers.
evidence: Cal's two runs took Mutineers, the only Initiation and both Spree picks, but he gained only 24 in round III and finished last.

subject: Goes Last token
claim: The token passing back and forth, with skipped turns, is hard for a new player to follow.
evidence: The token was taken 5 times in round I alone, and Dee lost track of whose turn was next at [38].

subject: Markdown
claim: Markdown's 2 off can come off a member's colored part, which the card does not say.
evidence: Dee bought Copyist (2 green + 3 any) with 3 blue at [185], and Ava's Latecomers cost 1 purple + 3 blue.

subject: Right Away
claim: The last placement of round I is often a leftover space, and Right Away on a last minion does nothing but give resources.
evidence: Cal's On a Roll and Dee's Right Away at [41] and [44] were both taken for 2 purple only.

subject: Gather
claim: Grey counts as a color for Gather's "a color you already have" but not for Purists' "2 or fewer colors".
evidence: Dee's Gather paid +4 for the grey Alchemists because she held grey members, while Cal's red-and-grey cult counted as 1 color for Purists.

subject: Green Cloak
claim: A copy of a copy pays the Green Cloak twice.
evidence: Dee's Reprise of her Cover copying Recruit Twice paid +2 green and +2 blue on top of the +5 blue.

subject: Borrow
claim: A borrowed member is a free shield against effects that make you discard one of your members.
evidence: Cal discarded his borrowed Loyalists to Purifiers in round I, losing nothing, while Ben and Dee each lost a real member.

subject: Spree
claim: Green's copies let one round III center space be used by three players in the same round.
evidence: Cal's Spree was copied by Ava's Echo and Dee's Cover: 5 discard-pile recruits and 21 blue from one space.

subject: Purists
claim: A swap that hands you a member of a new color switches off Purists, and a rival can do it on purpose.
evidence: Ben's Promote put purple Closer in Cal's cult, which with Cal's blue Repossessors made three colors and cost him the round III +3.

subject: Round end
claim: Round III's contest outcomes were settled by Red's swap spaces on the last placements, with no reply possible.
evidence: The Blue tie, the Red three-way tie and Purists switching off all came from Cal's Demote and Ben's Promote in the round's last six placements.

subject: Most members
claim: Most members rewards any body, so members bought only for their count decide it.
evidence: The round III 8-to-8 tie rested on Purifiers, Alchemists, Extra Hand, Seat Filler and Loyalists, none of which used its ability.
